clue.text: A view first seen in Virginia

indicators.note: seen in says one piece appears inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
first is written 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone recalls their earliest glimpse of a fine prospect while in Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is the container signal; the figure 1 in the ordinal 1st is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a pleasing prospect or outlook, a stretch of scenery seen from one spot.

clue.text: Doesn't get wrecked on the coast of Belgium

indicators.note: gets wrecked says the letters of the preceding word are smashed and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A ship somehow avoids running aground off the Belgian shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets wrecked' rearranges DOESNT (the apostrophe is ignored) into the seaside port's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a ferry port and resort town that lies on the North Sea shore of Flanders.

clue.text: Jumbos of a type now largely obsolete

definitions.text: Jumbos of a type now largely obsolete

parts.words: Jumbos of a type now largely obsolete
parts.note: reads like old jumbo jets being retired, but means elephants of a huge kind that died out; largely hints at their great size

explanation.surface: An aviation note on wide-bodied jets being phased out of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbos' suggests aircraft; it is the nickname for elephants, and 'largely' doubles as 'on a large scale', the extinct woolly giants.
explanation.definitionFit: These were huge prehistoric elephant relatives, now extinct, so obsolete jumbos on a grand scale.

clue.text: Just the boy to raise oil production!

definitions.text: Just the boy to raise oil production!

parts.words: Just the boy to raise oil production!
parts.note: a boy's first name that is also the tall lifting frame set over an oil well

explanation.surface: A recruiter praises a young lad as perfect for boosting an oilfield's output.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'boy' is a name, and the same word is a crane-like tower used to hoist drilling gear at a well.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a given name and the framework of girders over an oil well that lifts the drill pipe.

clue.text: Old Spanish coin mother and I raved over

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: over is read as overturned, so the letters of I and raved are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A child tells of how mum and they gushed about some antique peseta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' works as an anagram signal in the sense of turned over; mother comes first, as in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The maravedi was a low-value copper coinage of medieval and early-modern Spain.

clue.text: A Dickens book shattered this dream

indicators.note: shattered says the letters of the phrase are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A reader laments that a Dickens novel ruined their fond hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' rearranges THIS DREAM into the title of the 1854 novel set in Coketown.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard Times is a Charles Dickens novel of 1854 about industrial Coketown.

clue.text: He gets involved with sailors making North Sea investments, maybe

indicators.note: gets involved with says the letters of the two words are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A man goes into business alongside some seamen on an offshore venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets involved with' shuffles HE and SAILORS together; 'maybe' marks the definition as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Stakes in petroleum companies are a typical investment tied to drilling in the North Sea.

clue.text: Tropical bird with a bill in its stomach?

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other, here inside the stomach

parts.note: a maw is an animal's stomach or gullet
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A parrot has swallowed an invoice, or a bird's large beak seems lodged in its belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like the bird's beak, but it is an account; 'in' places it inside the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large, brightly coloured parrot of Central and South American rainforests.

clue.text: Part of the borough of York

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A guidebook mentions a district of the city of York.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'thE BORough'. Ebor, from the Latin Eboracum, is used as the signature of the Archbishop of York and in racing (the Ebor Handicap).
explanation.definitionFit: Ebor is the Latin-derived abbreviation meaning belonging to York, used in the archbishop's signature.

clue.text: Newspaper headline about a small river vessel?

definitions.meaning: a banner headline running across the full width of a page
read as ..., a vessel that sails a small river, as a steamer sails on steam

explanation.surface: A tabloid splash announces news about a little riverboat.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is invented: a small river is a stream, so a boat on one would be a stream-er; the question mark flags the coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner headline spanning a front page, and a whimsical name for a boat on a brook.

clue.text: South African currency brought in by an ardent spirit

indicators.note: brought in says the currency is placed inside the following word

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: Some foreign money is introduced by a zealous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts the currency inside the word 'by' itself. 'Ardent spirit' is an old phrase for strong distilled liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent spirits is an old term for distilled liquors, and this grape spirit is one such fiery drink.

clue.text: A side entrance of mine

parts.note: sounds like a person's private side door, but means a horizontal passage leading into a mine

explanation.surface: Someone points out the side door to their house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of mine' looks possessive ('belonging to me'); it means 'of a mine', a near-horizontal tunnel driven into a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal shaft driven into a hillside to give access to or drain a mine.

clue.text: Line followed by a genial essayist who was very fond of King Lear

definitions.text: who was very fond of King Lear

indicators.note: followed by says the next piece comes after the first

parts.note: a cord is a line or length of string
Elia was the pen name of Charles Lamb, the essayist

explanation.surface: A literary note on a writer of genial essays who was devoted to Shakespeare's king.
explanation.walkthrough: ELIA was the pen name used by Charles Lamb for his Essays of Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's tragedy, Lear's youngest daughter is the one who truly loves her father.

clue.text: Remain outside a coach in conformity with the law?

indicators.note: outside says the first word's letters go around the second

parts.note: to stay is to remain
a tutor is a private coach

explanation.surface: Someone stays out of a bus to stay within the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a bus but means a private teacher; 'outside' wraps the verb around him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something required or enacted by statute is in line with written legislation.

clue.text: He doesn't believe he is entering a motor-cycle race

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider who has no faith signs up for a motorbike race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the famous motorcycle road race on the Isle of Man; HE IS goes inside A TT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without belief in any god is a non-believer in religion.

clue.text: Sent abroad for money

parts.note: describes goods shipped overseas and sold to earn foreign currency

explanation.surface: Someone is dispatched overseas to earn a living.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a person posted abroad; the sense is goods sold to foreign buyers.
explanation.definitionFit: Products that are shipped out of the country for sale are trade goods sold overseas.

clue.text: A diver's dismayed counsellor

indicators.note: dismayed is used here as upset or thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frightened scuba diver seeks out someone for guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismayed' rearranges A DIVERS (the apostrophe is ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: A counsellor is one who gives guidance and advice to others.

clue.text: Closing date for protesting against a railway closure?

parts.words: for protesting against a railway closure?
parts.note: a closed railway is a ..., a date fixed to protest about it

explanation.surface: Campaigners set a cut-off date for objections to a branch line shutting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plain; the rest reads the word as dead line, a railway route no longer running.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-off time is the last date by which something must be done.

clue.text: Branches of the animal kingdom

parts.note: reads as divisions of zoology, but means the branching bony growths on a deer's head

explanation.surface: A biology lesson on the major divisions of zoological classification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branches' suggests taxonomic groups; it means the tree-like horns of stags.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the bony, branching headgear grown by deer, looking like boughs on an animal.

clue.text: Decline to make way for a successor?

definitions.meaning: to decline is to go down a stage
to resign a post so another can take it over

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to retire to let a younger person take over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like 'refuse' but is the first sense, going down a level.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to descend: a lowering in level, or resigning from office to let another take charge.

clue.text: Ring-road going round a hop-kiln

indicators.note: going round says the first pieces surround the next

parts.note: a ring is the shape of the letter O
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: A ring road loops around a kiln used for drying hops.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is the brick kiln, often with a cone roof, used in Kent for drying hops for brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops before they go to the brewery.

clue.text: What the criminal may get away with after a break-out?

definitions.text: What the criminal may get away with after a break-out?

parts.words: What the criminal may get away with after a break-out?
parts.note: the thing a fleeing crook escapes in, a getaway car

explanation.surface: A question about what a convict might get away with after escaping jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get away with' suggests avoiding punishment; it means escaping in, a getaway vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is another word for a motor car, the vehicle a robber uses for a getaway.

clue.text: Went after fresh detail

indicators.note: fresh says the letters of the next word are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone pursued a new detail in an investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges DETAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To have followed someone closely, as a detective shadows a suspect.

clue.text: Not up, not down, not true

definitions.text: Not up, not down, not true

parts.words: Not up, not down, not true
parts.note: of a light or garment switched or worn, neither raised nor lowered, and a pretence that is false

explanation.surface: A gnomic riddle listing three negatives.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase put on covers each: not put up, not put down, and assumed or feigned, as a put-on accent is not genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretended manner is feigned or affected rather than sincere, and the phrase also means placed or donned.

clue.text: Supplies moved quickly into a ship

indicators.note: into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a ship
tore means rushed or moved quickly

explanation.surface: Provisions were rushed aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: SS (steamship) holds TORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Provisions kept for later use are supplies held in reserve.

clue.text: Marlene's place, we hear, for the little people

indicators.note: we hear says the words sound like the answer when spoken

parts.note: Lili is the girl of the song Lili Marlene, and put means place

explanation.surface: A remark about where Marlene Dietrich kept something for children.
explanation.walkthrough: Lili Marlene is a wartime song, so Marlene's first name is Lili; with put (place) it sounds like the island of Swift's tiny people. The definition names the people for their land.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gulliver's Travels the island of tiny inhabitants is named for and stands in for its six-inch folk.

clue.text: It can't exist when there's anarchy or Red revolution

definitions.text: It can't exist when there's anarchy

indicators.note: revolution suggests overturning, so the letters of the phrase are turned about

explanation.surface: A political slogan that lawlessness or communist uprising destroys a calm society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges OR RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawlessness is the absence of civil discipline and regulated government.

clue.text: Cunningly crept in on an American university

indicators.note: cunningly says the letters are cleverly rearranged

explanation.surface: A sly intruder sneaks onto an Ivy League campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunningly' rearranges CREPT IN ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton is an Ivy League institution in New Jersey.
